utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Good morning. May I have the appearances, please, for the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases, my name is Niemann. I appear for the prosecution, and with me is Mr Tieger, Miss Hollis, who is not here today, Mr Fenrick and Mr Keegan of counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Niemann, and who is appearing for the defence, please? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: My name, Ms President, is Wladimiroff, and also here is Mr Vujin. Those are the lawyers in this case. We are assisted by Miss Feddes, Miss Starreveld, Mr Kollen and Mr Emile van der Does. They are assisting the defence on matters of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Wladimiroff. One additional comment, Mr Wladimiroff. I understand that Mr Tadic has completed an initial application for appointment of counsel? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: And that he has selected you as his first choice to represent him, and the Registrar has appointed you as counsel; is that your understanding? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: You will then be acting, so to speak, as lead counsel for the defence. That means that the Tribunal will send you notices, and send you notices as well, Mr Vujin, but we will be looking to you to tell us that you have received the notices, Mr Wladimiroff. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: For practical reasons, that will be a very good idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That also goes for the prosecutor, Mr Prosecutor. You would then of course send notices to Mr Wladimiroff, and of course to Mr Vujin, but except Mr Wladimiroff -- and pardon me if I am stumbling over the pronunciation -- Mr Wladimiroff is the lead counsel. Do you understand that, Mr Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the prosecutor ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the prosecution is ready to proceed in the case against the accused, Tadic. In relation to the accused, Borovnica, who is also mentioned in the indictment, a warrant for his arrest has been issued, but he is still at large. Accordingly, unless he is arrested in the immediate future, we would wish to proceed to trial against the accused, Tadic, at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is the defence ready to proceed? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: For the record, then, Mr Borovnica is not present today?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Just Mr Dusan Tadic; is that correct, Mr Wladimiroff? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Wladimiroff would you wait a moment? I would like to speak to you. Has Mr Tadic received a copy of the indictment? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: He has, Ms President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Has Mr Tadic read the indictment or had it read to him in a language he understands? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: He did read it in his native language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Have you discussed the indictment with Mr Tadic? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: Not extensively, but just a global discussion has been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you believe that Mr Tadic under-stands the nature of the charges contained in the indictment? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: I think he understands the nature of the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: And I see, Mr Vujin, you are nodding your head as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is Mr Tadic ready to agree with the indictment for the purposes of entering a plea, or would he be willing to waive the reading of the indictment? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: He is willing to waive without any prejudice to the contents of it, but he does not need to have the indictment read extensively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: When you say, "waive", I do not mean waive any of his rights to plead not guilty to the indictment. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is exactly what I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Just not a formal reading of the indictment? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Tadic, would you please stand? For the record, would you state your full name, please, as well as any other names that you may have gone by? THE DEFENDANT: Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Are there any other names that you have gone by, Mr Tadic? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: We cannot hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Tadic, for the record, would you state your full name. THE DEFENDANT (original: Serbian): I do not understand English. I only understand the Serbian language, and I only speak the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Can you hear me now, Mr Tadic? THE DEFENDANT: (original: Serbian): I already said that I do not understand the English language. I do not have an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Tadic, for the record, would you state your full name? THE DEFENDANT: My full name is Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Have you gone by any other names, Mr Tadic? THE DEFENDANT: (original: Serbian): I never used any other names, except my closest friends sometimes called me Dule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Tadic, are you ready to enter a plea to the indictment? THE DEFENDANT: (original: Serbian): Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How do you plead to the indictment; guilty or not guilty. THE DEFENDANT: (original: Serbian): Not guilty, and I never took part in any of the crimes with which I am charged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: I understand then, that by pleading not guilty you are pleading not guilty to each and every of the charges contained in the indictment; is that correct? THE DEFENDANT: (original: Serbian): I did not take part in any of the crimes with which I am charged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: You are pleading not guilty to each of the charges; is that correct? THE DEFENDANT: (original: Serbian): Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr Tadic, you may be seated. Are there any preliminary matters that we need to discuss, lawyers, before we determine a date for trial? First, Mr Prosecutor, are there any preliminary motions that you intend to file?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We will be seeking to file one motion so that there may be a hearing under Rule 75(B) of the Rules in relation to the taking of evidence by victims who have been sexually assaulted and who we propose would give evidence in these proceedings. We suggest that we would be in a position to file our papers in this matter by about the 18th May, if that is a convenient date for the Tribunal, with the matter then proceeding to a hearing at some subsequent date after that. The situation is, your Honour, that some of these witnesses that we seek to rely on are at the moment unable to bring themselves to give evidence in the traditional manner, so we would be seeking to rely on the provisions of 75(B) of the Rules in order to overcome that issue. At the moment, that is the only preliminary motion that the prosecution wishes to identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you contemplate that you would require a hearing for that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be that the Tribunal would be assisted by a short hearing. I imagine that we would file a fairly detailed documentary motion, but that the specific Rule itself, 75(B), seems to contemplate some sort of hearing, and we have in mind at this stage -- and I must say it is not settled -- calling perhaps some evidence by experts in this field who may be able to assist the Tribunal with resolutions of questions. So, to that extent, there may be a necessity for a hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Niemann. Mr Wladimiroff, suppose we give you -- I am trying to count the dates here -- until the 2nd June. I think that would be about 14 days. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: I do not think that will be enough Ms President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: How much time do you think that you would need, Mr Wladimiroff? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: I think two weeks more would be convenient for the defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Two weeks in addition to the 14 days? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That would then get us to about June 18th, I suppose. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: That is a Sunday. Therefore, I would have waited until the following Monday Actually I was thinking about pushing it back the other way. Of course, I have not seen the motion, and neither have you, so you do not really know whether you would need a month. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: There is some difference between the prosecution and the defence, that we have not yet had a disclosure of the file, so we cannot judge the context of it. For that reason, I think we need some more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Suppose we gave you two weeks initially, let you look at the motion and, if you need an additional two weeks, then, of course, we would be happy. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is a good idea, yes. We can agree to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Then you would respond to the motion, we will say, by the Monday, which would be June 5th.Actually, that is a little bit more. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That will be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Wait a minute now. That is even too much time. Excuse me, this is April 26th. Let us count the days. Why do we not give you until Friday, May 12th to file your response? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: At least to file a response with respect to the date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Attempt to file a response to the motion that the prosecutor indicates that it is filing. If you do not have enough time after you have received the motion, and you consider that you are unable to respond to it in that approximate two week period, then simply file a request for leave for an additional two weeks. It may be that, when you receive their motion, you will find that you can easily respond to it. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: Yes, I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: You may have, then, until May 12th, with the understanding that, if, after you have received the motion, you need additional time, then you will advise the Court prior to that time, and we will attempt to give you that additional time that you need. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Wladimiroff, do you intend filing any preliminary motions for the defence? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: Yes. Within the terms of the 60 days' motions, we are considering, but not decided yet. So we are not able to tell you at this stage which motion we will file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: The rules of procedure and evidence do give you 60 days, of course, to file the motions. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: We will do that as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: For how long has Mr Tadic has been in custody in Germany? Since February of last year? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUJIN
utterances.text: He is okay with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Then you will have 60 days to file the motions. In all likelihood, Mr Wladimiroff, we will schedule a pre-trial conference or a status conference, so to speak, with counsel only, perhaps in two weeks, just to get a feel for where you are. Perhaps by then you will be in a better position to tell us what motions you will be filing, and when you might be filing them. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: We would appreciate that, if we could have such a meeting, because we are all dependent on the file we have not yet seen. It merely is a practical problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Let me count my dates on my calendar again. We will set a status conference for May 11th at 10.00 am for the purpose of discussing the preliminary motions. We certainly hope, Mr Wladimiroff, that on that date you will be in a position to give a good indication of what motions you intend to file, if you can, only so that we can schedule them accordingly. But you are not required; you are correct, you do have the 60 days. Mr Niemann, when do you expect that you will provide the defence with the papers that accompany the indictment as required by the rules?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: To answer your Honour's question, we are expecting to provide the defence with a bundle of material today. There is some material that we have not provided, because it is affected by our application, but apart from that everything else will be supplied today. Your Honour, while I am on my feet, I notice that when discussing the dates, your Honour mentioned 12th May as the response date. I assume your Honour meant 12th June?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Actually, we do not have 12th June. What I have done is to give counsel for the defence two weeks to respond, and, if he needs more additional time -- from what you are telling me, you think that he really will need more time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I am sorry, there was a misunderstanding. It is just I have noticed from this wonderful device that records the transcript, that when there was mention of the dates, I suggested that I would file my notice of motion by 18th May, and then your Honour was discussing the times for the defence to respond. Your Honour mentioned 12th May. Just for the record, I assume your Honour means 12th June. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: I see what you mean. There might be some confusion about dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Do you need a month, Mr Wladimiroff, to respond to the Government's motion? You saying that that is what you are thinking, but I thought we agreed that until you really received the motion, it is difficult for you to tell. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: What we are trying to say is that, after we have received the motion, we will need 14 days and maybe an additional 14 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Okay. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: That is it. It just depends on the date the motion will be filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Mr Niemann, then you will be filing your motion on May 18th, and then counsel for the defence will have 14 days to respond to it. I will let someone else, who is better with calendars, compute those dates; 14 days after they file their motion, which they are filing on May 18th. If you need additional time after that 14 days, then of course you may ask for leave, and we will take a look at it at that date. If someone has a calendar and they can do the computation better than I, Miss Featherstone, perhaps you can come up with a date 14 days after the 18th. Mr Wladimiroff, the Court Clerk tells me that your response then would be filed on June 2nd. That is the response to the prosecutor's application that we will be filing on May 18th. Again, if you need additional time, then please advise the court. PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: We appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: We had then set a status conference for May 11th at 10.00 am. The purpose of the status conference will be for the lawyers to meet with the Tribunal to discuss preliminary matters further. Is there anything else that we need to discuss preliminarily?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, nothing by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: The defence, anything else? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Is the prosecutor ready to proceed to trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Defence? PROFESSOR WLADIMIROFF: We are, Ms President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: The Tribunal will not set a date for trial at this time. A trial date will be set after we resolve the motions. Of course, we are not certain at this point what motions we will be receiving, but as soon as we receive the motions and the responses and resolve them, I will ask that the Registrar set a date for trial. Are there any additional matters that need to be discussed?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Not from the point of view of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Court is adjourned. (11.00) (Court adjourned) 23 24 25
